issues.title: Rental deposit not returned
issues.description: Your landlord or hostel has not returned your security deposit.
steps: Collect your rental agreement, payment proof, messages and move-out evidence.
Send a calm written request listing the amount, date and a reasonable response deadline.
If unresolved, contact a legal services authority or a qualified lawyer to understand the suitable next step.
issues.note: Rental rights depend on the agreement, state law and the facts of the situation.

issues.title: Unpaid internship or overtime
issues.description: You believe promised internship payment or wages have not been paid.
steps: Keep the offer letter, internship terms, attendance, timesheets and payment messages.
Ask the organisation in writing to clarify the amount due and the payment date.
If the issue continues, seek advice from the relevant labour authority or a legal services provider.
issues.note: Whether a payment or labour law applies depends on the work arrangement and applicable law.

issues.title: College disciplinary action
issues.description: You want to challenge a disciplinary decision or understand a college complaint process.
steps: Read the student handbook, notice and applicable university regulations.
Keep copies of notices, emails and evidence; note any appeal deadline.
Submit a factual written representation through the official college or university grievance process.
issues.note: Follow the rules and appeal process applicable to your institution. Seek advice for serious or urgent matters.

issues.title: Online purchase or service complaint
issues.description: A seller or service provider has not resolved a purchase or service problem.
steps: Save the invoice, order ID, screenshots, warranty and communication.
Contact the seller or service provider and clearly state the resolution you want.
If unresolved, check the National Consumer Helpline and its current complaint process.
issues.note: The helpline offers consumer grievance support; it does not guarantee a particular outcome.

issues.title: Privacy or misuse of personal information
issues.description: You are concerned about how an organisation or person used your personal information.
steps: Save relevant messages, screenshots, dates and account/security notifications.
Use the service's official privacy, grievance or security reporting channel.
If there is a threat, fraud or immediate safety concern, contact the appropriate official authority.
issues.note: The correct process depends on the type of data, who used it and the circumstances.

flashcards.title: Keep a paper trail
flashcards.body: Save agreements, receipts, emails, notices and dated screenshots. Organised records can help you explain a problem clearly.

flashcards.title: Read before you sign
flashcards.body: Read agreements and ask for unclear terms in writing before accepting them. Keep a copy of the signed version.

flashcards.title: Ask for the process in writing
flashcards.body: For a college grievance, ask which policy applies, how to submit a representation and whether a deadline exists.

flashcards.title: Know where to ask for help
flashcards.body: NALSA and State/District Legal Services Authorities provide information about free legal services and eligibility.

flashcards.title: Consumer complaints need evidence
flashcards.body: Keep order details, invoices, payment proof and a record of the attempts you made to resolve the issue.

resources.name: NALSA — Legal Services
resources.description: Information about free legal aid and legal services authorities.
